invalid_failure_risks: Binary extraction in Bash on large datasets: if scripts/extract_spool.sh parses binary frames via bash loops and subprocesses (e.g., dd, od, xxd), processing the 50,000+ frame fuzz test will cause severe performance timeouts on 1 vCPU.

Percentile interpolation method ambiguity: multiple linear interpolation variants exist (e.g., R-6, R-7 / NumPy default, R-8). Any discrepancy between the shell script implementation and the test verifier's exact formula will fail tests.
Socket draining termination: tests using `--stream-socket` may hang if EOF, timeout, or shutdown signaling semantics on the live UNIX socket are not explicitly defined.
Rust build resource limits: compiling dependencies from scratch on 1 CPU / 2 GB RAM can take several minutes or trigger OOM kills unless artifacts are pre-warmed in `target/`.
review.reasons: The blueprint presents a challenging and realistic debugging scenario spanning binary protocol alignment, payload reassembly, timestamp wraparound arithmetic, and statistical aggregation. The difficulty stems from genuine multi-stage causal dependencies rather than trickery. With proper environment pre-warming and explicit mathematical definitions in the spec, this forms a high-quality hard task.
fixes: Ensure `extract_spool.sh` delegates binary splitting to a fast compiled utility or vectorised tool rather than pure bash loops so that 50k+ frame fuzz tests complete within seconds.
Explicitly document the exact percentile formula in `docs/SPEC.md` (e.g., specify method type such as R-7 / NumPy linear interpolation: index = (N - 1) * p with linear weighting between values).
Pre-compile all Rust dependencies inside `target/release/deps` in the container image so that running `cargo build --release` only recompiles the pipeline crates (~5-10s on 1 vCPU).
Clarify socket stream termination semantics in `docs/SPEC.md` (e.g., stream drains until socket EOF or daemon shutdown signal).
